chunks: As for whatever is in it from Mismaʿ ibn Mālik al-Baṣrī, I have transmitted it from my father—may Allah be pleased with him—from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from Abān, from Mismaʿ ibn Mālik al-Baṣrī.

And it is said of him: Mismaʿ ibn ʿAbd al-Malik al-Baṣrī, and his لقب was Kurdīn. He was an Arab from Banū Qays ibn Thaʿlabah and was known by the kunya Abū Sayyār. And it is said that al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said to him when he first saw him: “What is your name?” He said: “Mismaʿ.” He said: “Son of whom?” He said: “Son of Mālik.” He said: “Rather, you are Mismaʿ ibn ʿAbd al-Malik.”

key_terms.الْبَصْرِيِّ: A native or affiliate of Baṣrah; identifies his regional attribution.
key_terms.كُرْدِينُ: The epithet by which he was known.
key_terms.يُكَنَّى أَبَا سَيَّارٍ: He was known by the kunya Abū Sayyār.

ai.seo_question: What is the sanad to Mismaʿ ibn Mālik al-Baṣrī in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh, and who was he?
ai.summary: This passage gives the transmission chain for reports narrated from Mismaʿ ibn Mālik al-Baṣrī and then provides brief biographical information about him. It also records a report that Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام identified him as Mismaʿ ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, clarifying his lineage and naming.
